report.subject: Algorithmic Substrates vs. Declarative Snapshots
report.content:
The fundamental divergence between Markdown/SVG and DOCX/PDF lies in the nature of their 'backends.' Markdown and SVG are algorithmic substrates; they represent instructions that require a programming language backend (Parser/Renderer) to instantiate their final form. Conversely, DOCX and PDF are declarative snapshots; they represent finalized states intended for passive consumption by static layout engines.

Markdown does not exist as a visual entity until it is processed by a logic-heavy backend. The renderMarkdown function demonstrate that every Markdown symbol is a trigger for a programmatic conditional. SVG backends allow for direct manipulation via JavaScript. An SVG is a living branch of the DOM tree, whereas a PDF is an opaque binary blob.

DOCX and PDF represent the 'Legacy Substrate'—formats designed to hide their logic and present only the artifact. Word processors like Google Docs or Microsoft Word are optimized for consumer experience and printing but sacrifice the integrity and legibility of the underlying artifact (the asset), making them unsuitable for professional outputs that require agents to efficiently process information. The ideal format for agents is JSON because of its tree structure, which allows agents to grab only specific lines for processing.

As codified in the LexClinic Office Hours (2026-01-14), interacting with agents must be viewed as operating heavy machinery, requiring full attention and care. This necessitates safeguards against destructive agent capabilities (like .git folder deletion). The 'We Do' system utilizes algorithmic substrates to turn the 'firehose into a garden creek' through fractal sharding and sophisticated agent loops (e.g., .we.do.json naming conventions).

Versioning is an intentional snowballing process. A high-quality report typically requires around 13 versions to reach a satisfactory quality. This WeDo instance serves as Version 1, established under the mandate of forensic commit trails.
